context_excerpt: 2025-10-26 **Event**: Country X's Forces B issued a statement on October 26, warning that if Country Y's President Leader A carries out his threat to attack Country X's energy facilities, Country X will completely close Strait A. Leader A posted on social media on October 25 that if Country X did not reach an agreement with Country Y on the nuclear issue, Country Y would carry out "unprecedented bombing" of Country X…

time.desc: One party announced that it had initiated direct dialogue with its opponent and pledged to temporarily suspend military strikes on its opponent's energy facilities to create a diplomatic window
One side formally submitted a plan to end the conflict containing multiple clauses to its opponent, aiming to promote ceasefire negotiations to break the deadlock.
The counterparty submitted a formal response to the multi-term ceasefire plan, bringing the ceasefire negotiations into a new stage of advancement.
The warring parties carried out joint attacks on port facilities close to key maritime energy channels and caused casualties, highlighting the military escalation of shipping nodes
Major countries outside the region jointly proposed a multi-point plan to end the war, calling for an immediate ceasefire and the restoration of normal access to key sea lanes.
In a national address, leaders of one side announced tougher military strikes against their opponents in the coming weeks and stressed the goal of ending the conflict as quickly as possible.
The two warring parties launched a new round of joint air strikes on the opponent's important petrochemical industry and export hubs, further attacking the opponent's energy and industrial base.

One side publicly threatened to attack its opponent's civil infrastructure such as power and transportation, while the opponent warned of possible expansion of the blockade of key sea lanes as a counterattack.
One side agreed to suspend bombings and attacks on its opponents and set a ceasefire period of about two weeks to provide a window for diplomatic negotiations.

After the ceasefire came into effect, the allies made it clear that the ceasefire did not cover their actions against certain disputed armed forces/regions, triggering disputes over the scope and sustainability of the ceasefire.

The military of one party officially launched a blockade of the opponent's ports and maritime trade, and stated that it would not prevent ships related to non-opponent ports from passing through key sea lanes.

The leader of one of the parties involved in the war publicly called on all countries to go to the key strait to rush to transport oil, claiming that the opponent had been basically defeated, and related oil prices rose sharply late at night.
Opponents held large-scale commemorations for forty days after the death of the supreme leader. The successor supreme leader said that his country shocked the world during the war.

The navy of one of the participating parties began to mobilize troops to key straits and prepare to blockade the opponent's ports. The actions were carried out at the same time as the talks between the two sides.
